summary: Wood County, Texas tower registered 2014 as US 986, TX 3; believed 70-foot tower with 7x7 Aermotor cab, now a radio repeater site; no build or staffing records found.

facts.design: Believed to be a 70-foot tower with a 7 by 7 foot Aermotor cab

evidence.supports: administered by Texas A&M Forest Service

evidence.quote: This is believed to be a 7'x7' Aermotor cab on a 70-foot tower.

evidence.supports: cab now houses a radio repeater
evidence.quote: It currently houses a Texas A&M Fire Service radio repeater.

evidence.supports: community about ten miles southeast of Quitman
evidence.quote: ten miles southeast of Quitman in southeastern Wood County

evidence.supports: community at the intersection of three farm roads
evidence.quote: at the intersection of Farm roads 14, 49, and 312

evidence.supports: sawmill community Liberty Hill as early as 1850, southeast of the later town site
evidence.quote: As early as 1850 a sawmill community called Liberty Hill was located slightly southeast of where Pine Mills would later stand.

evidence.supports: timber depleted and mills moved away by about 1905
evidence.quote: by about 1905 the local timber was depleted, and the mills moved away

sources.title: Pine Mills, TX
sources.publisher: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas

notes_for_editor: Only the NHLR page describes the tower itself, and it hedges with 'believed'. No build date, builder, staffing, fire or access record was found in NHLR, TSHA, firelookout.org, or the Forest Lookouts regional page (which shows only the name). NHLR says 'Texas A&M Fire Service' for the repeater, probably meaning Forest Service; the story quotes it as the Register's wording. height_m is 70 ft converted. Brief coordinates match firelookout.org. Access is left out because no read source states it; brief 'unknown' stands. Not checked: Texas A&M Forest Service records or local newspapers. Confidence medium because registry and standing agree across sources, but history is thin. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'Sawmills came first' overstated the TSHA entry (which gives 1850 as the earliest date; a church and school followed by 1854-55), so it now gives the 1850 date; the Register footnote was removed from the advice sentence; the farm-road and registry-number evidence was added.
